title: Théorie des cycles algébriques : conjectures de Hodge, Tate, Lefschetz, Weil : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
The scan is upside down. It is page 7 of an English typescript, not a page in Grothendieck's hand. It is unrelated to the surrounding manuscript notes on Alb/Pic and on abelian varieties with cycle rings, and is presumably a stray sheet from a preprint by another author. The notation is the author's own: the double-underlined A denotes a category of commutative algebras, and the axioms are numbered 1°, 2°L/R and 5°.

The problem is to classify the cogroup objects, i.e. Hopf-algebra or affine group-scheme structures, on the polynomial ring A = K[t].

1. Write the comultiplication as m(t) = Σ α_ij t^i⊗t^j.
2. Normalize so that the counit is e_F(t) = 0.
3. The dual left and right unit axioms (2°L, 2°R) then force m(t) = t⊗1 + 1⊗t + Σ_{i,j>0} α_ij t^i⊗t^j, i.e. a polynomial formal group law F(x,y).
4. Coassociativity, F(F(x,y),z) = F(x,F(y,z)), gives equation (3.1).
5. Leading-term argument. Let p be the largest first index with some α_pj ≠ 0, and q the largest second index among those.
   - On the left, the term α_pq·m(t)^p⊗t^q contains α_pq^{p+1} t^{p²}⊗t^{pq}⊗t^q. Its first-factor degree is p².
   - Every term on the right has first-factor degree at most p.
   - So p = 1, or else all α_ij = 0. Symmetrically, the largest second index is 1.
6. Hence m(t) = t⊗1 + 1⊗t + α t⊗t.

This is the classical fact that a polynomial one-dimensional formal group law over a field is x+y+αxy. That is the additive law, or, after rescaling when α≠0, the multiplicative law x+y+xy. The argument still works in characteristic p, because Frobenius preserves the leading monomial. The next page of the typescript is not available, so the conclusion and the antipode step cannot be seen.
errors: The argument tacitly uses that K is a field, or at least reduced or integral. Over rings with nilpotents the leading coefficient α_pq^{p+1} could vanish, and more polynomial group laws exist.

Potential gap: the visible part never imposes the antipode (inverse) axiom. For α ≠ 0 the law x+y+αxy has inverse −x/(1+αx), which is not a polynomial. So K[t] with that comultiplication is only a bialgebra (a monoid scheme, the multiplicative monoid shifted), not a Hopf algebra. A true cogroup structure on K[t] forces α = 0, i.e. G_a. Whether the author handles this on the next page (perhaps through e_A or axiom 5°) cannot be checked.
Minor: the notation e_A : A → A with e_A(t) = 0 is unexplained on this page.

ideas.what: Classification of comultiplications on K[t] (one-dimensional polynomial group laws) via a leading-degree argument applied to coassociativity
ideas.modern_name: Polynomial formal group laws / Hopf algebra structures on K[t]; G_a (and G_m as a monoid law x+y+xy)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Lazard, Dieudonné; standard in formal group and Hopf algebra texts, e.g. Hazewinkel)
ideas.where_published: Related material is in SGA 3 (affine group schemes); this specific typescript is not Grothendieck's.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a stray page of someone else's English typescript giving a routine, classical classification of polynomial group laws on K[t]. It has no connection to Grothendieck's own notes in this folder and nothing new.
transcription_corrections: The page image is rotated 180°, and the sheet is a typewritten English text rather than a manuscript of Grothendieck.
The term on the left-hand side reads α_pq α_pq^p (t^p ⊗ t^q)^p ⊗ t^q, as transcribed. This is correct, since m(t)^p contains (α_pq t^p⊗t^q)^p.
In the right-hand line of the associativity equation, the handwritten insertion '+α_ij+' is an α_ij written in by hand over the typed sum Σ t^i ⊗ m(t)^j.
A small handwritten mark ('ht' or similar) appears in the corner of the sheet.
